entries.title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
entries.abstract: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($μ$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $μ$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $μ$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.

entries.title: Refining the Architecture of the Quadruple Pre-main-sequence System HD 98800: Improved Orbits, Dynamical Masses, and a Transiting Circumbinary Disk
entries.abstract: We present new spectroscopic and interferometric observations of the pre-main-sequence hierarchical quadruple system HD 98800, a member of the nearby TW Hya association. Our radial velocity monitoring extends the total coverage to over 36 years, sampling the periastron passage in the $\sim$240-yr outer orbit. By combining these velocities with new and archival interferometric observations of both inner binaries (A and B), we significantly refine the system orbits and constrain the dynamical masses of all four stars to $\leq$ 2.6 percent. The resulting stellar properties (masses, effective temperatures, and absolute magnitudes) are found to agree well with current stellar evolution models. Notably, binary B hosts a known circumbinary disk in a polar orientation. Our interferometric imaging, as well as ground-based photometry by others, capture binary A currently passing directly behind the disk, a striking alignment given the outer orbit's long period. We use the photometry to infer the optical extinction produced by the disk material. The eclipse is expected to last about a decade, and offers an unprecedented opportunity to probe the structure and composition of the potentially planet-forming disk. Our refined orbits and component masses provide a robust dynamical framework to support ongoing and future studies of this unique event.

entries.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
entries.abstract: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

entries.title: AGN feedback in the multiphase inner intracluster medium of a cosmological super-resolved galaxy cluster
entries.abstract: The intracluster medium (ICM) of galaxy cluster cores is a multiphase environment regulated by active galactic nuclei (AGN) feedback. Extended cool gas nebulae with complex morphologies and kinematics are commonly observed in cool-core clusters, but their origin and interaction with AGN feedback remain poorly understood. We present a cosmological magnetohydrodynamical zoom-in simulation of a low-mass cool-core galaxy cluster ($M_{\mathrm{200c}}=2.3\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$), using initial conditions from TNG-Cluster and the IllustrisTNG galaxy formation model. Through super-Lagrangian refinement, we achieve a baryonic mass resolution of $2.3\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and a spatial resolution of $\sim40\text{-}90$ pc in the cool ($10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}<T<10^{5.5}\,\mathrm{K}$) gas phase within the central $370$ ckpc, while retaining the full cosmological context. We investigate the properties and evolution of cool clouds and filaments and their interaction with AGN feedback at $z\leq0.35$. The cluster core hosts a rich population of dense, low-entropy filaments, including inflowing and outflowing structures and occasional rotationally supported disks. Comparing simulations with AGN kinetic feedback turned off and on, we find that AGN activity fragments and redistributes the cool gas and increases its covering fraction without destroying the cool gas reservoir. Individual outbursts drive transient increases in the velocities and velocity dispersions of both cool and hot gas, on short, $\lesssim 50$ Myr, timescales. We also identify low-entropy gas uplifted by AGN-driven outflows. While feedback globally heats the ICM and offsets cooling, it also creates conditions that may favor local thermal instabilities -- through shock compressions, mixing, turbulence, and uplift.

entries.title: Low-excitation molecular gas in a Ly$α$-associated companion of the $z=4.7$ quasar in BR1202-0725
entries.abstract: Quasar companions at high redshifts are usually gas-rich star-forming galaxies whose molecular gas masses ($M_{\mathrm{mol}}$) are estimated from [C II], dust emission or a single mid-$J$ CO line. We detect CO(5-4) and [C I](1-0) with ALMA in LAE-2, a Ly$α$-associated companion of the $z=4.7$ quasar in BR1202-0725, and CO(5-4) at the location near LAE-1, the Ly$α$ emitter between the quasar and the submillimeter galaxy (SMG). With the CO(2-1) flux from the literature, LAE-2 has an $L'_{\mathrm{CO(5-4)}}/L'_{\mathrm{CO(2-1)}}$ ratio of $0.22\pm0.04$, as in high-redshift main-sequence galaxies but four times lower than in the quasar host and the SMG. A non-LTE model places the CO(5-4) excitation temperature only 4 K above the cosmic microwave background (CMB), yet the same gas would show an even lower ratio against the $z=0$ CMB. The CMB-corrected $M_{\mathrm{mol}}$ from [C I], $\approx9\times10^{10} M_{\odot}$, agrees with the independent [C II] estimate, whereas CO(5-4) gives a four times lower mass if assumed thermalized at 40 K with the same CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor. Combining our 3 mm measurement with archival far-infrared photometry, we find cold ($\approx25$ K) dust and main-sequence star formation, with a gas-to-stellar mass ratio of $\approx4$ and a depletion time of $\approx0.7$ Gyr. Its star formation can supply the far-ultraviolet field that the [C I], [C II], and CO lines require. Quasar companions can thus retain massive, weakly excited molecular gas reservoirs that mid-$J$ CO surveys can miss.

entries.title: Euclid: Discovery of a quasar at z = 8.13 hosting a 360-million-solar-mass black hole
entries.abstract: Quasars powered by rapid accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have been uncovered deep into the first gigayear of cosmic history. We present the discovery of EUCL J150452.291+625224.39 (J1504+6252), selected from Euclid Wide Survey imaging and spectroscopically confirmed as the first quasar at z > 8 through observations with Keck, HST, LBT, and JWST. J1504+6252 exhibits the defining spectral signatures of archetypal quasars at lower redshift, including a luminous blue power-law continuum and broad permitted emission lines, indicating a classical broad-line region. JWST/NIRSpec G395M spectroscopy yields a systemic redshift of z = 8.129 +/- 0.005, corresponding to 630 Myr after the Big Bang and shifting the quasar redshift frontier by about 39 Myr (6% of the age of the Universe at that epoch). From H-beta and Mg II, we measured intrinsic broad-line-region FWHM of 3160 +/- 270 and 3740 (+160/-170) km/s, respectively. A widely used single-epoch H-beta calibration gives a reference black hole mass of log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.56 +/- 0.43. Applying a range of calibrations to both Mg II and H-beta yields log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.33-8.89 and Eddington ratios of 0.12-0.44. Assembling a black hole of several hundred million solar masses within the first few hundred million years, despite its currently sub-Eddington accretion rate, requires either a massive seed or sustained, highly efficient early growth. The discovery of a mature, sub-Eddington quasar at z > 8 suggests that substantially more luminous quasars hosting similarly massive black holes may remain to be discovered. Conversely, previously known reionisation-era quasars may represent the rapidly accreting end of a broader population of already massive black holes spanning a wider range of accretion states.

entries.title: Probing the X-Ray Structure of the $z = 2.38$ Strongly Lensed Quasar J1721+8842, the First Einstein Zig-Zag Lens, Down to $140\ \mathrm{pc}$
entries.abstract: Sub-kiloparsec X-ray structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN), including outflows, jets, and dual AGN, provide key insights into their evolution and influence on host galaxies. In the local universe, Chandra X-ray Observatory's state-of-the-art $0.5''$ angular resolution has resolved these structures, but at $z > 0.1$, milliarcsecond resolution is required to spatially resolve sub-kpc scales. We leverage the spatial amplification by strong gravitational lensing to investigate the X-ray structure of J1721+8842, a $z=2.38$ quasar lensed into six images. To reconstruct the optical emission position, we model the lensing mass distribution using the six quasar images, five detected by Gaia Data Release 3 (A-E) and one by HST (F). Our model reproduces the five Gaia image positions to milliarcsecond precision. To locate the X-ray emission relative to the optical, we combine ray-trace simulations of archival Chandra observations with the lens model image position predictions using a double maximum-likelihood analysis. We constrain the X-ray centroid within a $0.017''\times0.004''\ (139\times30\ \mathrm{pc})$ ellipse centered $0.005''\ (44\ \mathrm{pc})$ away from the optical source position. Source-plane reconstructions of the soft-X-ray and hard-X-ray to optical sources demonstrate these emission regions are cospatial, allowing the optical source at $1σ$ confidence. These results indicate no evidence for kpc-scale X-ray jets, outflows, or dual AGN with projected separations exceeding $140\ \mathrm{pc}$. This method improves Chandra's effective angular resolution by a factor of 30 at cosmological distances, enabling studies of sub-kpc AGN X-ray structure at cosmic noon.

entries.title: The hot circumgalactic medium: implications of mixing and resolution at the disk-halo interface
entries.abstract: We demonstrate that microphysical processes at the disk--halo interface, typically unresolved in circumgalactic medium (CGM) simulations, strongly affect the thermodynamic structure and observational signatures of an inflowing hot ($\sim10^6\,{\rm K}$) CGM. If the hot gas is pulled through the interface faster than it can cool, e.g.\ by turbulent mixing with the ISM or fountain flows, the hot CGM approaches an isentropic state. If instead the interface is regulated by radiative cooling on the hot gas cooling time, the hot CGM develops an outward-increasing entropy profile akin to a classic cooling flow. The two regimes differ by a factor of $\sim\!10$ in the predicted hot gas density above the disk near the rotation axis, and consequently by a factor of $\sim100$ in the predicted X-ray emission measure. We show that an isentropic CGM is produced in idealized CGM simulations that fail to resolve the pc-scale disk--halo interface, as numerical mixing drives artificially rapid cooling at the interface. A similar isentropic structure is found along the rotation axis in FIRE zoom-in simulations of $z\sim0$ Milky-Way-mass galaxies, where the cooling layer is likewise unresolved, raising the possibility that numerical mixing contributes to the isentropic structure. In contrast, an outward-increasing entropy profile forms in our idealized simulations when we replace the unresolved interface with an inner boundary that enforces a slow inflow. This outward-increasing entropy profile is likely also present in the Milky Way hot CGM, inferred from comparing density estimates at $\sim100\,{\rm kpc}$ with the entropy of the eROSITA bubbles.

entries.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
entries.abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}σ$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

entries.title: Revisiting TOI-2120 b: Updated mass and radius constraints on a sub-Neptune orbiting an M4 dwarf
entries.abstract: We present updated mass and radius measurements of TOI-2120 b, a short-period (5.80 days) planet orbiting a mid-M dwarf identified by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). TOI-2120 b was previously validated through transit photometry and high-resolution imaging, with a radius near the upper boundary of the radius valley around low-mass stars. We refined the planetary properties by combining archival TESS and ground-based photometry with new transit observations from the ARC 3.5m and Red Buttes Observatory (RBO) telescopes and new precision RV measurements obtained with the Habitable-zone Planet Finder (HPF) spectrograph. Our joint analysis yields a radius of $2.31\pm0.7$ Rearth, larger than previously reported. We also measure a planetary mass of $5.81^{+2.94}_{-2.69}$ Mearth at 2$σ$, corresponding to a bulk density of $2.62^{+1.37}_{-1.22}$ g cm$^{-3}$, positioning TOI-2120 b toward the water-rich region predicted by isocomposition models. Additional RV observations will be needed to further constrain its mass and composition.

entries.title: From residuals to warps: Probing disk geometry with gas kinematics
entries.abstract: Evidence of shadowing among protoplanetary disks suggests that warped protoplanetary disks are widespread, making it crucial to constrain their three-dimensional shape in order to understand their dynamical evolution and origin. Yet, inferring this warp shape from observations is challenging, as the typical signatures of a warp, especially shadows, are often degenerate with the warp shape. Kinematics of disks may provide a method to recover the shape by interpreting the residuals from a Keplerian disk model as local changes in inclination and position angle. In this work, we test its applicability and limitations. We perform radiative transfer simulations of disks with a parametrized warp shape to create synthetic maps of $^{12}\mathrm{CO}$ rotational line emission at ALMA wavelengths and compare the fitted warp with the true warp shape. We find that the warp shape can be recovered for nearly face-on disks with small warp misalignments of a few degrees, even without knowledge about disk properties such as emission height. The overall warp shape remains traceable even at moderate spectral resolutions up to $0.8\,\mathrm{km/s}$. However, we identify regimes where the method breaks down, including disks with an inclination higher than $40^\circ$, a high emission height of the tracer, and sharp warp transitions. In addition, radial and vertical motions can introduce apparent warps and twists, motivating extensions of the method to account for these effects.

entries.title: The SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project: Time-delayed Variability of a Quasar's C IV Broad Absorption Troughs
entries.abstract: Broad absorption line (BAL) quasars offer a powerful view into the structure, kinematics, and feedback mechanics of active galactic nuclei. In this study, we track the dramatic behavior of intrinsic CIV outflows of the quasar SDSS J142129.40+522752.0 at z = 3.228. We analyze 199 high-signal- to-noise optical spectra collected over a 12-year baseline via the Sloan Digital Sky Survey III/IV Reverberation Mapping and the SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping programs. We quantify multi-year variability across two prominent absorption features: a primary high-velocity CIV BAL trough (Trough A) and a lower-velocity mini-BAL (Trough B). Both troughs exhibit rapid, significant variations in equivalent width and average depth, culminating in temporary disappearances during the 2022-2023 observing seasons before reappearing at their original velocities. We find that the behavior of the two troughs is highly correlated with both the g-band flux and each other, strongly indicating that the observed variability is driven by ionization state changes of the gas. The equivalent width of the mini-BAL Trough B is found to lag that of Trough A by ~4 days in the quasar rest frame, suggesting that the equilibrium timescales of the two absorbers are different and possibly indicative of different outflow densities or distances.

entries.title: A Meta-analysis of Chemical Abundances Derived from Ultraviolet and Optical Lines of Os, Ir, and Pt, and a Reassessment of the Robustness of the Third r-process Peak in Metal-poor Stars
entries.abstract: We reassess the abundance ratio between elements at the third rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) peak (Os, Ir, Pt) and the lanthanide element Eu. We show that some weak optical lines of Os I, Ir I, and Pt I yield abundances inconsistent with stronger ultraviolet (UV) and optical lines and provide recommendations for their limited use alongside more reliable lines. We perform a meta-analysis of Os, Ir, and Pt abundances from 35 studies of 77 r-process-enhanced metal-poor stars spanning -3.43 < [Fe/H] < -1.27 and +0.22 < [Eu/Fe] < +2.45. The mean third-peak to lanthanide abundance ratios are $\log\varepsilon$(Os/Eu) = 0.86 $\pm$ 0.02, $\log\varepsilon$(Ir/Eu) = 0.88 $\pm$ 0.03, and $\log\varepsilon$(Pt/Eu) = 1.12 $\pm$ 0.04, which agree with the inferred Solar System r-process ratios to within 0.05 dex. These abundance ratios vary by less than 0.50 dex (a factor of 3.2), 0.56 dex (a factor of 3.6), and 0.45 dex (a factor of 2.8), respectively, in 90 percent of the r-process events that enriched metal-poor stars in existing samples. We use a representative r-process model to show that the small range of stellar abundance ratios favor models with a substantial contribution from neutron-rich material, with electron fractions, $Y_e$, < 0.2. We conclude that the third-peak to lanthanide abundance ratios are robust in existing r-process-enhanced star samples. In two stars with [Eu/Fe] < 0, the upper limits derived from non-detection of Pt indicate that the third-peak elements are deficient relative to lanthanides, and we conclude that this may be a signature of the limited r-process.

entries.title: Constraining the Leptonic and Hadronic Contributions to the Gamma-Ray Emission of SNR HESS J1731-347 with CTAO Forecasts
entries.abstract: We present a Bayesian broadband spectral analysis of the supernova remnant HESS J1731-347, combining archival radio, X-ray, and H.E.S.S. data with a new analysis of 16 yr of Fermi-LAT observations. The LAT data allow the GeV emission of the western molecular-cloud core (MC-core) to be separated from that of the remaining shell. We fit purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models with and without the MC-core region. Within a one-zone model with fixed distance and ambient density, the lepto-hadronic scenario is strongly preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) in both cases. Excluding the MC-core, we obtain $Δ{\rm BIC}=33.67$, a magnetic field of $B = 84.9^{+27.5}_{-22.9}$ $μ$G, a hard proton index of $α_p = 1.69 \pm 0.10$, and a proton energy of $W_p = (4.37^{+0.64}_{-0.51})\times10^{48}$ erg for $n_{\rm H}=20$ cm$^{-3}$. The preference for a hadronic contribution is therefore not driven by the MC-core emission alone. CTAO simulations show that a 50 h observation with the southern array would detect the source at $13σ$ to $18σ$ and substantially improve the constraints on its TeV spectrum.

entries.title: H$_3^+$ forbidden rotational lines in a planetary nebula: JWST/MIRI detection in the Ring Nebula and ionization by the central star
entries.abstract: We report the detection of the forbidden pure rotational spectrum of H$_3^+$ in the Ring Nebula (NGC 6720), to our knowledge the first detection of H$_3^+$ in a planetary nebula. In JWST/MIRI spectra obtained toward the inner edge of the main ring, 0.1 pc in projection from the central star, the $(J,K) = (5,0)\to(4,3)$ line at 16.325 $μ$m is detected at $32σ$, along with nine further unblended lines. The H$_3^+$ emission spatially follows the H$_2$ emission, whose rotational lines show warm (660 K) and hot (1700 K) components. A statistical-equilibrium model at these temperatures reproduces the subthermal H$_3^+$ line pattern, with much of the emission arising in the hot H$_2$. The emission requires an H$_2$ ionization rate of $\sim 3\times 10^{-12}\,{\rm s^{-1}}$ in the hot H$_2$ for an electron fraction of $2\times 10^{-4}$. The rate is $\sim 2\times 10^4$ times the cosmic-ray ionization rate in diffuse clouds. The extreme-ultraviolet and soft X-ray radiation (54-300 eV) of the 135 kK central star supplies this rate if the hot H$_2$ lies within an H-nucleus column density of (4-8)$\times 10^{19}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$ of the ionization front of the dense globules. Static photoionization models, however, place the H$_2$ in gas too cold to excite the H$_3^+$ lines. The warm molecular gas and its H$_3^+$ thus suggest dynamical effects, most plausibly the advection of H$_2$ through a photoevaporation front into gas heated by the star. H$_3^+$ provides a new probe of the photoionization of molecular gas by very hot stars.

entries.title: Multi-vantage SO/PHI and SDO/HMI magnetic field observations of active region NOAA 13465
entries.abstract: Context. Until the launch of Solar Orbiter, long term studies of active region magnetic fields were restricted to a single vantage point: that from Earth. What further restricted these studies were geometrical effects, such as foreshortening and projection, that plague magnetic field observations when the active region was away from the central meridian. Aims. To track an active region, in this case NOAA 13465, with Solar Orbiter during a perihelion pass and use co-observations made by SDO/HMI and SO/PHI-HRT from different vantage points to explore the systematics plaguing observations away from disc centre. Methods. We use the SHARP (Space-Weather HMI Active Region Patches) data series from SDO/HMI, and create similar datasets with SO/PHI-HRT observations. We compare and contrast the line-of-sight and the three heliographic magnetic field components. Finally we compare the unsigned radial flux, and unsigned totals of the northward and westward magnetic components using the SHARP masking method to select a common area. Results. We find that the instrument observing closer to the limb infers a greater unsigned radial magnetic flux compared to that observing at disc centre, with a maximum near approximately $45^\circ$. The plage displayed more susceptibility to resolution and projection effects than the active region's sole sunspot. In particular the deduced area of the solar plage drove the observed increase in flux near the limb. Thanks to its higher spatial resolution, the SO/PHI-HRT data showed a smaller effect compared to SDO/HMI near the limb, highlighting a dependence on instrument resolution. Finally, the ratio of the two instruments' vertical magnetic flux exhibits a strong positive correlation with the ratio of the cosine of the instruments' viewing angles.

entries.title: Clumping Factor in the Mix: Incomplete Mixing Suppresses Turbulent Reaction Boost
entries.abstract: Cosmological simulations often account for unresolved density fluctuations using a sub-grid clumping factor when modeling chemical reactions. To validate this approach, we conduct hydrodynamical simulations of isothermal, supersonic turbulence and track the evolution of passive chemical species in first-, second-, and third-order reactions, exploring seven reaction rates across Mach numbers $M$ = 2-50 in three turbulence driving modes. We parametrize the saturation of clumping factors at $M \gtrsim 10$ due to intermittency (i.e., falling significantly below the log-normal prediction) with a one-parameter fitting formula. Furthermore, we find that the competition between turbulent mixing and the density-dependent reaction rates, governed by the Damköhler number (Da), suppresses the global reaction rate by a \textit{mixing efficiency} factor ($ξ$). For Da $\ll 1$, chemical species remain well mixed ($ξ\to 1$), and the reaction rates are boosted by a clumping factor. For Da $\gg 1$, reactants in dense gas are rapidly depleted before being redistributed by turbulence, causing $ξ$ to drop by a factor of a few to more than an order of magnitude. We quantify the effective mixing efficiency as a function of two dimensionless parameters, $M$ and Da, and provide a fitting formula that can be easily adopted in cosmological simulations to accurately follow unresolved chemical reactions.

entries.title: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters
entries.abstract: Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited, in addition to the fundamental, pressure, and gravity modes. While direct observations of the oscillation spectrum remain challenging, potential resonance signatures from these modes could be manifested in the precursors of short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron star mergers. If the oscillation spectrum is observed, this is a good opportunity to extract the physical properties through the technique of asteroseismology. In particular, we focus on the crustal elasticity and examine the $s$- and $i$-mode frequencies. We find that, for a given EOS specified by the nuclear saturation parameters, the radius-scaled $s$-mode frequencies and the mass-scaled $i$-mode frequencies can be expressed as a function of the stellar compactness, independently of the stiffness of the core EOS, at least when the EOS in a higher-density region can be characterized only by the specific constant sound velocity. Then, we could derive the fitting formula for the $s_i$-mode for $i=1-4$ and $i_1$-mode frequencies as a function of the stellar compactness and the combination of the incompressibility of symmetric nuclear matter, $K_0$, and the slope parameter for the nuclear symmetry energy, $L$. If the $s$- and/or $i$-mode oscillation frequencies were observed, one may get the relation between these properties by identifying the observed frequencies with specific modes, using our fitting formula, which offers useful insights into the nuclear saturation parameters and stellar properties. By combining the other observational data, it may be possible to narrow the parameter space of EOS parameters and stellar properties. We emphasize that this article summarizes the results presented in our previous studies and discusses their implications for neutron star seismology.

entries.title: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
entries.abstract: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.

entries.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
entries.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

entries.title: The Eclipsing $γ$ Doradus Star VZ Canum Venaticorum
entries.abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the eclipsing binary VZ CVn using TESS Sectors 50 and 77 photometry together with published spectroscopic results. The TESS light curves were modeled to refine the binary parameters, and the residual light curves were analyzed to investigate the pulsational properties of the system. We derive masses and radii of $M_{\rm A}=1.526\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm A}=1.638\pm0.023$ $R_\odot$ for the primary and $M_{\rm B}=1.259\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm B}=1.133\pm0.016$ $R_\odot$ for the secondary. Comparison with PARSEC evolutionary models suggests a near-solar metallicity of $Z=0.017$ and an age of 1.0 Gyr. Separate frequency analyses of the two TESS sectors reveal four signals with possible counterparts in both sectors. Two of these frequencies, $f_2=4.7486$ day$^{-1}$ and $f_6=7.1242$ day$^{-1}$, are consistent with the fourth and sixth orbital harmonics, respectively, suggesting an orbital origin rather than independent $δ$ Sct pulsations. The dominant frequency $f_1=1.7577$ day$^{-1}$ has a pulsation constant of $Q_1=0.336$ day, consistent with a $γ$ Dor-type g-mode pulsation. The weaker signal $f_5=1.9754$ day$^{-1}$ also has a pulsation constant of $Q_5=0.299$ day, although its detection remains tentative because of its low S/N. Together with the physical and evolutionary properties of the primary, these results support its classification as a $γ$ Dor pulsator rather than the previously proposed $γ$ Dor--$δ$ Sct hybrid pulsator.

entries.title: A Wideband Technosignature Search of 210,191 Nearby Main-sequence Stars with the VLA Sky Survey
entries.abstract: Searches for radio technosignatures have concentrated on narrowband signals. We present a complementary search for excess broadband 2-4 GHz emission from 210,191 Gaia DR3 main-sequence stars within 100 pc in all epochs of the VLA Sky Survey (VLASS; 2017-2026). Cross-matching with the Epoch-1 catalog yields 51 high-reliability positional associations (versus 1.5 expected by chance). All but one are known natural emitters that, where measurable, move with their stars; the remaining source, near LSPM J1943+5337, is not at the star. Because stellar flares can mimic transmitters in continuum flux, a detection counts as a possible transmitter at any luminosity only at the 32,985 apparently single AFGK stars outside known radio-emitter classes, and at M dwarfs and AFGK multiples only above $10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Forced photometry of 208,232 stars in all epochs finds 1 steady-test detection and 3 stars detected in at least one epoch among the eligible stars, against 1.3 and 1.9 expected by chance. The median per-star limit on steady emission is $L_ν<4.0\times10^{8}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Without background subtraction, fewer than $1.5\times10^{-4}$ of eligible AFGK stars host a steady transmitter above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$, and fewer than $2.3\times10^{-5}$ of all stars outside the known-emitter classes host one above $\sim1.1\times10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$; counting every M-dwarf detection as a possible transmitter, fewer than $5.5\times10^{-4}$ of M dwarfs host one above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Stacks detect population-averaged emission from M dwarfs, concentrated in those with activity evidence. Continuum surveys thus constrain broadband, modulated, or rapidly drifting signals that narrowband pipelines do not search for.

entries.title: Quiet-Sun magnetic field configuration inferred from the ratio of longitudinal fields measured in the Fe I λ6301 and λ6302 Å lines
entries.abstract: The estimate of the longitudinal magnetic field obtained from the Hinode spectropolarimeter data will be different if it is determined in different ways. In particular, the values obtained by the Center Of Gravity (COG) method for the Fe I $λ$ 6301 and 6302 $Å$ lines do not coincide. Some of the differences are due to the different inaccuracies of the COG method for each of the two lines. However, some of the differences can be explained by the fact that the response functions of these lines to changes in the magnetic field are formed at different heights. This should be accompanied by a certain morphological structure of magnetic fields. It consists in the fact that most of the magnetic configurations of the quiet photosphere are similar to each other. To a rough approximation, their structure can be compared with the structure of a sunspot - there is a central region with the strongest field, close to vertical, and slopes - an analog of penumbra, where the field weakens and / or turns to horizontal. This turn occurs at the heights of the greatest response of the Fe I $λ$ 6301 and 6302 $Å$ lines to changes in the magnetic field with a turn length of about tens of kilometers.

entries.title: Nonlinear models of Mira variables with long secondary periods
entries.abstract: Calculations of nonlinear radial oscillations in asymptotic giant branch stars with an initial mass of $M_\mathrm{ZAMS}=1.6M_\odot$ were performed for initial helium and metal abundances of $Y=0.28$ and $Z=0.006$, respectively. Several models from the evolutionary sequence after the 4th thermal pulse were used as initial conditions for the hydrodynamic equations describing stellar pulsations with long secondary periods. Using the discrete Fourier transform of the hydrodynamic solutions we show that long secondary periods appear in Mira variables pulsating simultaneously in the fundamental mode and first overtone with non-multiple periods. The relative deviation from multiplicity is $δ_\mathrmΠ\le 1.2\times 10^{-2}$ and is responsible for mode splitting into equally spaced frequency components, each of which is a standing wave with a free outer boundary. The cycle length of long secondary periods is nearly 20 times that of the fundamental mode. Long secondary periodicity is a nonlinear effect that arises after reaching the limiting amplitude and develops over several hundred fundamental mode periods.

entries.title: Electron processing of glycine: evidence for peptide-forming condensation reactions
entries.abstract: The discovery of amino acids on asteroids, including samples returned from asteroid Bennu, and the detection of glycine on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko support the hypothesis that glycine can form in extraterrestrial environments. Laboratory experiments show that glycine can form through both energetic and non-energetic processing of interstellar ice analogues. In the interstellar medium, glycine is exposed to various forms of energetic processing, including cosmic rays and the secondary electrons they generate, which have been shown to produce complex organic molecules, including peptides. This work investigates whether peptide-forming chemistry is a general consequence of energetic processing. Films of glycine and glycine-d3 were grown in two ultrahigh-vacuum chambers and irradiated with 1-2 keV electrons. The irradiated samples were subsequently characterised using infrared spectroscopy, temperature-programmed desorption, and vacuum-ultraviolet spectroscopy. Peptide formation through condensation reactions would produce water as a secondary product, and spectra obtained following irradiation of glycine-d3 showed evidence of D2O formation, supported by TPD measurements, which revealed H2O formation for glycine and H2O, HDO, and D2O for glycine-d3. VUV spectra of irradiated glycine showed the formation of decomposition products, including CO and CO2, as well as H2O. Following heating, a non-volatile residue remained on the surface. Electron irradiation of glycine produces reaction products similar to proton irradiation, suggesting that the resulting chemistry is not strongly dependent on the energy source. These findings support the possibility that larger organic molecules can form in a wide range of extraterrestrial environments. Such molecules may subsequently be incorporated into small bodies and delivered to planetary surfaces, potentially contributing to the emergence of life.

entries.title: Robustness of Transition Probabilities of Spectral Lines Deduced from Spatially Resolved Solar Spectra
entries.abstract: Atomic parameters are a key ingredient for the synthesis of spectral lines to model observed spectra and to extract meaningful physical information about the observed astrophysical object. We use quiet-sun observations to test the reliability of the atomic parameter inference from observed spectra. Our focus is on the transition probability of spectral lines, denoted as log(gf). We apply a spectropolarimetric inversion method to quiet-sun disc-centre observations at 1.56 $μ$m from the GRIS/GREGOR spectrograph. We use the coupled method implemented in the globin inversion code, where atomic parameters are spatially coupled, and a single value of these parameters is determined for every spectral line over the entire field of view. We carry out tests to determine the sensitivity of the inferred log(gf) values to various atmospheric parameters and the data reduction fallibility. We find that our log(gf) values are weaker by 0.023 dex compared to the most recent study. This is most probably caused by the constraint imposed on the log(gf) parameter due to the spatial coupling, lifting the degeneracy between temperature and log(gf). We use the Markov chain Monte Carlo method to determine the uncertainty in the inferred log(gf) values. For the strongest lines in the spectral region, the uncertainty in log(gf) is 1-4 %, increasing to 12 % for weaker and blended lines. Our tests suggest that the log(gf) values inferred using the coupled method from globin are robust against any local contamination to the observed line profiles, such as spectral stray light, and return a reliable and unique set of log(gf) values for the strongest lines irrespective of the chosen atmospheric model and observation dataset. This result is valid as long as the underlying assumptions of line formation under local thermodynamic equilibrium and the completeness of the line list are satisfied.

entries.title: The evolution of discs and the epoch of formation of giant planets around low-mass stars
entries.abstract: Large-grain depletion in the inner discs of young stellar systems provides a potential observational signature of dust filtration by forming giant-planet cores. In a previous study, we found that $0.50\pm0.10$ of prominent protoplanetary discs around solar-type stars ($0.7$--$1.5$~\Msun) with ages of 2--8~Myr show evidence for a depletion of large grains inside the snow line. Such a depletion may arise when a sufficiently massive planetary core acts as a barrier to the inward drift of large grains, filtering them from the inner disc. If this interpretation is correct, the frequency of dust-filtration signatures should decrease towards lower stellar masses, in accordance with the lower occurrence rate of giant planets around low-mass stars. Extending our analysis to lower-mass stars, we found that only $0.09\pm0.09$ of discs around stars with masses of $0.30$--$0.58$~\Msun, corresponding to the progenitors of main-sequence early M-type stars, show evidence of grain filtration. This fraction is lower than that measured for solar-type stars and is consistent with the lower frequency of giant planets around M-type stars. We also found that discs exhibiting evidence of filtration tend to have relatively massive outer dust reservoirs, with dust masses exceeding $20$~\MEarth. Conversely, the absence of filtration signatures in lower-mass discs suggests that Neptune-mass and lower-mass planets, despite being common around low-mass stars, may generally be unable to filter large grains efficiently.

entries.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
entries.abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

entries.title: Photometric Characterisation and Evolutionary State Investigation of the Low Mass-Ratio Contact Binary FASTT 1558
entries.abstract: Contact binaries with low mass ratios, as potential progenitors of stellar mergers, offer important insights into the physical processes governing mass and energy transfer. In this work, we present the first spectro-photometry based evolutionary investigation of FASTT 1558, a totally eclipsing, low mass-ratio contact binary. We combine TESS and ASAS-SN photometry with phase-resolved spectroscopy obtained with the 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope. The lightcurve modeling with PHOEBE shows that the system has an exceptionally low secondary-to-primary mass ratio of $q=0.1544\pm0.0013$, with a deep contact degree of $f=0.61\pm0.01$. Our analysis yields a total system mass of $1.92\pm0.31\,M_\odot$, while the distance to the system is estimated to be $648.45\pm29.85$ pc. Analysis of long-term eclipse timings reveals an apparent orbital period decrease of $\dot{P}=-(3.03\pm0.26) \times 10^{-7}$ ${\rm day\,yr^{-1}}$, which may be associated with mass-transfer from the primary to the secondary on a thermal timescale. The spectra show phase-dependent H$α$ and CaII equivalent widths, indicating a dynamically evolving chromosphere. Binary evolution calculations with MESA terminates through L2 overflow before reaching the observed low mass-ratio. Despite its extreme mass ratio, the system is presently Darwin stable, with $J_{\rm spin}/J_{\rm orb}=0.15\pm0.02$. FASTT 1558 therefore provides a robust observational benchmark for evolutionary models of low mass-ratio contact binaries.

entries.title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: multi-band dust continuum observations reveal heavily obscured starbursts among UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$
entries.abstract: Detailed studies with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) have shown that dust is widespread even in UV-luminous galaxies at $z\gtrsim6.5$. Multi-band continuum observations are critical to fully characterize these early dust reservoirs. We present a homogeneous analysis of multi-band ALMA observations from the REBELS Large Program and seven follow-up programs, targeting thirteen massive galaxies at $6.5\lesssim z\lesssim7.7$ in at least two bands, including Band 8. Through optically thin modified blackbody fitting, we infer the dust masses, temperatures, and infrared luminosities of our targets. Their dust temperatures span $T_\mathrm{dust}\approx30-70\,\mathrm{K}$, and a stack reveals an average $T_\mathrm{dust}=49_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{K}$. Three sources nominally qualify as ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; $L_\mathrm{IR}>10^{12}\,L_\odot$), with total star formation rates of $\mathrm{SFR}_\mathrm{UV+IR}\approx160-300\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the highest of which is found in our most distant target, REBELS-18 at $z=7.67$. Their star formation is heavily obscured, with $\gtrsim90\%$ emerging in the infrared, compared to an already large average obscured fraction of $f_\mathrm{obs}=0.75\pm0.11$ for the stack. These SFRs are consistent with the reconstructed growth histories of some massive quiescent galaxies at $z\approx4-5$, suggesting that dusty yet UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$ are plausible progenitors of such systems. The sample moreover displays large dust-to-stellar mass ratios ($M_\mathrm{dust}/M_\star = 0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}\%$), best reproduced by models in which dust grows efficiently in the interstellar medium. This demonstrates that a dust-rich, IR-luminous, and heavily obscured galaxy population is already in place well into the Epoch of Reionization.

entries.title: The dust attenuation scaling relation in the TNG50 simulation
entries.abstract: The infrared excess (IRX = L_IR / L_UV) of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) follows a tight scaling relation with star formation rate, gas-phase metallicity, and size up to z ~ 3, providing a key benchmark for galaxy formation models. We test whether TNG50 SFGs, post-processed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT, reproduce the universal IRX relation - linking IRX to metallicity, infrared luminosity, size, and inclination - and identify the origin of any offsets. We analyse 7280 TNG50-SFGs across 0 <= z <= 4, comparing their predicted IRX relations with observations and the EAGLE simulation. We test different dust-to-metal (DTM) ratios and dust compositions, recalibrate galaxy properties to observed scaling relations, and decompose the offsets into individual parameter contributions. TNG50-SFGs match the universal IRX relation closely at 0.5 <= z <= 1, but lie above it at z = 0 (+0.5 dex) and below it at z >= 2 (-0.25 dex). They follow a relation of the same functional form, with a shallower, metallicity-independent L_IR slope. At z ~ 0, TNG50-SFGs are ~1 dex fainter in L_IR than the local calibration sample, requiring extrapolation; at fixed stellar mass and L_IR, simulated and observed IRX agree within 0.04 dex. At z >= 2, TNG50-SFGs are less obscured than predicted, an offset largely removed by lowering their metallicities by ~0.2 dex. Varying the DTM ratio and dust type shifts the offset normalisation without resolving its redshift evolution: a redshift-dependent DTM ratio helps at high z, but not at z = 0. Resolving the low-z discrepancy requires both improved dust models and observational constraints on IR-faint galaxies.

entries.title: The Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) Survey I: Photometric Calibration of NB395 and Metallicity Estimation
entries.abstract: We present the first results of the Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) survey, a narrow-band photometric survey targeting metallicity-sensitive narrow bands using the Hyper Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope. This paper outlines the scientific goals, survey strategy, current observational status, photometric calibration, and metallicity estimation. The current ZERO footprint comprises 21 pointings, covering approximately 35 deg$^2$ along the celestial equator in the NB395 band, reaching NB395 $\sim$ 24.5 mag (10$σ$) in one hour, significantly deeper than typical comparable narrow-band Ca H\&K surveys. The NB395 photometry is calibrated using corrected Gaia BP/RP spectra and the recalibrated SDSS Stripe 82 catalog, achieving a typical zero-point precision of $\sim$0.3 per cent and flat-field precision better than 1 per cent on spatial scales larger than 8$^\prime$. Under typical conditions (three repeats; total exposure time $\sim$1 hour), the photometric precision reaches $\sim$1.1 per cent at NB395 $\approx$ 12, $\sim$1.5 per cent at 20, and $\sim$10 per cent at 24. We estimate [Ca/H] using a Physics-constrained Stellar Locus Fitting Method. The resulting [Ca/H] precision is better than 0.18 dex for sources brighter than NB395 $\sim$ 20, spanning a wide metallicity range from metal-rich to the very metal-poor regime ($-3 \le$ [Ca/H]$\le +0.5$). We further show that NB395 traces [Ca/H] more directly than [Fe/H]. The final catalog contains one million sources with NB395 photometry, including 379,216 repeatedly observed and 61,845 with [Ca/H] estimates. These results provide a solid foundation for future ZERO survey, including photometric calibration, stellar parameter determination, and investigations of Galactic structure and chemical evolution.

entries.title: A catalog of Gaia DR3 luminous blue variables and candidate luminous blue variables
entries.abstract: Galactic LBVs are rare, evolved massive stars whose defining evidence is long-term spectroscopic and photometric instability, including S Doradus-type cycles, and, in exceptional cases, giant eruptions. Candidate LBVs (cLBVs) share LBV-like spectra and/or circumstellar nebulae; however, they lack long-term observational datasets that would detect their long-term variability and confirm their classification as bona fide LBVs. Modern time-domain surveys provide homogeneous light curves for many Galactic massive stars, but each survey has its own limitations in terms of depth, temporal coverage, and observing cadence. Using confirmed Galactic LBVs as a control sample, we aim to test what Gaia DR3 and complementary photometric surveys can and cannot establish about LBV-type variability. We assembled a vetted sample of 75 Galactic LBVs and cLBVs with near- and mid-infrared photometry from 2MASS, MSX, WISE, GLIMPSE, and MIPSGAL. The infrared material was used to validate identifications, evaluate source confusion, and place objects in a circumstellar-dust context. We then constructed light curves from Gaia DR3, the Bochum survey, the ASAS SN, and the ZTF, and analyzed large-amplitude and periodic cases with Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods. Gaia DR3 matches are available for 67% of the sample and 76% are reported as variable. We identify high-amplitude variables and periodic systems that may be binaries rather than classical LBVs. Six confirmed LBVs and five candidates show variations larger than 0.6 mag in the Gaia RP filter. Their light curves are examined and three periodic variables are identified. The light curves of OMN2000 LS1 and DWC2011 140 show primary and secondary minima, strongly suggesting eclipsing binary systems. OMN2000 LS1 has a well-constrained period of 80.29 d, and DWC2011 140 of 95.07 d.

entries.title: Critical Eddington luminosity and photon cooling of compact spherical stars
entries.abstract: Context. Relativistic corrections to the luminosity have been used for neutron stars of radius greater than $3MG/c^2$ in studies of X-ray bursts. However, there is no fundamental limit that excludes the existence of more compact massive objects with a physical surface, fluid or solid. Aims. We aim to discuss critical "Eddington" luminosity for spherical stars that have a surface within the sphere of unstable circular photon orbits (photon sphere). Methods. We use standard analytical ray-tracing formulae in the Schwarzschild metric. Results. We find that for stars within the photon sphere, the Eddington condition for balance between radiative force and gravitational attraction is fundamentally altered by photons returning to the surface. The equilibrium is non-local and requires stationarity on timescales of photon fall-back. As a result, spontaneous symmetry breaking is possible, leading to non-uniformity of emission across the photospheric surface. Conclusions. For a fixed intrinsic luminosity, the photons returning to the surface decrease the cooling rate of stars inside their photon sphere. At the same time, the returning photons increase the value of the critical luminosity that would balance gravity. One and the same redshifted formula applies to the critical luminosity, as seen by a distant observer, for any radius of the star. In the X-ray burst literature, for stars with radius less than 3 gravitational radii a different formula has long been accepted that missed the essential physics of the photons emitted in directions outside the escape cone.

entries.title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $α$-Element, and Age Dependencies
entries.abstract: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. By modeling the asymmetric color residuals relative to a metallicity-dependent single-star locus, we measure the binary fraction $f_b$ and constrain the power-law slope $γ_{\rm large\,q}$ of the mass-ratio distribution at high mass ratio $q$. Higher metallicity is associated with a steeper (more negative) $γ_{{\rm large}q}$, indicating a larger proportion of low-mass-ratio systems. For $α$-elements, [Mg/H] and [Si/H] are anticorrelated with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples; conversely, [Ca/H] shows a positive correlation with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples. No correlation is found between $f_b$ and $α$-element abundances in thick-disk-dominated subsamples. The binary fraction increases modestly toward older ages in the thin-disk population, a trend that likely reflects underlying correlations with chemistry. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.

entries.title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
entries.abstract: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. We consider two basic scenarios of CR origin: I) the supergalactic scenario assuming diffusion of the protons inside a magnetic field structure with the characteristic radius $H = 1-20$ Mpc and II. the cosmological scenario with the maximum redshift of the sources $z_{max} = 6$.

entries.title: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
entries.abstract: The $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. However, stellar-evolution systematic uncertainties from metallicity, rotation, and mass-loss prescriptions remain poorly quantified. Here we use the MESA stellar-evolution code to construct a three-dimensional parameter grid disentangling these coupled effects. We show that metallicity-dependent winds dominate helium-core retention; rotation suppresses carbon consumption via centrifugal cooling and meridional mixing; different mass-loss prescriptions produce $8$-$10\,M_\odot$ offsets in the black-hole-mass-gap edge. A parameter combination $Z\approx10^{-3}$, moderate rotation $ω/ω_\mathrm{crit}=0.4$, and optically-thin C15 winds reproduces the GWTC-4 inferred maximum primordial-black-hole mass for $S_{300}=108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$. The canonical $45\,M_\odot$ gap boundary represents an overlapping statistical intersection of black-hole-population distributions rather than a universal physical threshold. Our framework provides a pathway to jointly constrain nuclear-reaction rates, stellar-evolution physics, and gravitational-wave-source populations.

entries.title: The W Transform: an additional powerful tool for astrophysical time-series analysis
entries.abstract: This work introduces the W Transform (WT) for astrophysical applications and explores its similarities and differences to the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), in photometric stellar light curves (LCs). We tested both techniques on synthetic data, producing LCs with different noise levels and numbers of gaps, and applied them to LCs from TESS space mission. The analysis focused on six stars: the solar analog TIC 276293046, the ultra-cool dwarf TIC 359892714, the $γ$ Dor pulsator TIC 164173105, the eclipsing binary TIC 355151781, the hosting planet star TIC 142276270, and the brown dwarf TIC 102076870. Overall, the results were in agreement, except for stars with LCs presenting sector-to-sector differences in structures or changes in the number of gaps, reflecting time-dynamic effects in the same target, which affect how time-dependent variability features appear in the time-frequency representation. For such LCs, the WT spectra are more stable and accurate in recovering signal amplitudes than the CWT maps, which exhibit distortions and limitations, showing that the inherent flexibility of the WT method in adjusting the dominant frequency could enhance time resolution even in LCs with complex or variable structures. We conclude that the WT is a robust tool for the analysis of stellar LCs, and that both methods may complement each other in an in-depth analysis of a periodic astrophysical signal. The present results suggest that the WT is a robust and accurate tool for analyzing stellar LCs, expanding the range of numerical techniques available for analyzing different stellar periodic phenomena from photometric observations.

entries.title: The Alma catalog of OB stars. IV. A massive star census of the Magellanic Clouds System
entries.abstract: Context. The Magellanic Clouds System (MCS), comprising the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB), offers a nearby laboratory for studying massive stars. Existing catalogs are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature. Aims. We identify candidate stars with initial masses of roughly 8 solar masses or more, including O- and early-B-type stars, supergiants, luminous blue variables, and Wolf-Rayet stars. We aim to improve completeness in reddened and crowded regions and recover sources missed by large surveys. Methods. We combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical and infrared surveys. We select candidates using color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications. We check for duplicates and multiple systems, include literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts, especially in 30 Dor, and derive synthetic Gaia photometry where Gaia measurements are incomplete. Results. ALS IV contains 51 954 massive star candidates: 36 506 in the LMC, 15 264 in the SMC, and 184 in the MB. It provides homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and spectral classifications where available. Complementary photometry and HST observations recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selections. The sample traces the main massive-star populations and prominent star-forming regions across the MCS. Conclusions. ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.

entries.title: CORALIE Radial Velocity Search for Companions around Evolved Stars (CASCADES) VI. Revised masses and homogeneous estimation of the stellar parameters of 583 red giants
entries.abstract: Giant-star radial-velocity surveys allow us to study how the exoplanet population varies with stellar mass and evolution. However, obtaining accurate estimates of stellar masses for such stars is challenging, as methods like isochrone fitting are prone to large errors due to the degeneracy associated with the closeness of isochrones. We provide a homogeneous re-derivation of the stellar parameters of the CASCADES giant-star survey. This includes parameters obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, as well as an update of the stellar masses using asteroseismology. We use TESS light curves to measure the frequency of maximum oscillation power, $ν_{\rm max}$, for all the stars when applicable. We re-extract the stellar radii of the survey by fitting broadband photometry with ARIADNE, a spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting package, using priors from spectroscopy for the effective temperature, metallicity and $\log g$. By using scaling relations, we compute revised estimates of the stellar masses of targets with a $ν_{\rm max}$ measurement. We obtain new estimates of mass for 583 out of the 640 stars of the survey. These revised masses are typically 15 to 20% lower (median difference of $-0.35\,M_\odot$) than the ones obtained by isochrone fitting, in particular for low-metallicity stars for which this effect is stronger. These new masses impact the overall mass distribution of the sample, whose median decreases from $2.11\,M_\odot$ to $1.65\,M_\odot$. These revised masses provide the basis for future occurrence-rate analyses aiming to study the link between host-star mass and planet occurrence. They also highlight the uncertainties associated with the determination of masses for evolved stars.

entries.title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
entries.abstract: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. DG Tau's mid-infrared spectrum consists of a very bright continuum with various silicate features, and lines of CO, H$_2$O, OH, H I, H$_2$, Ne$^{+}$, Ne$^{2+}$, Ar$^{+}$, Fe$^{+}$, and Ni$^{+}$. We find substantial grain growth to at least 2 $μ$m at an early evolutionary stage. Lines of H$_2$O and CO are formed at extremely high temperatures (600-2000 K). The ratio of warm to hot water is the lowest among previous observations of disks with JWST. This and a very strong continuum point toward the relevance of the strong accretion of DG Tau and consequently strong stellar UV irradiation. The pair of jets reveals a rich spectrum of emission lines from ions, in particular producing forbidden lines of [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], and [Ni II]. The forward jet shows a collimated structure as found previously, while the hitherto poorly described, receding jet is more widely dispersed on scales of several arcsec, showing a layered structure with the fastest components being the most collimated. The ionization of the jet gas cannot be reconciled with high-energy radiation from the star itself. Instead, we propose a unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model in which the previously studied X-ray jet plasma continuously cools, recombining ions until, at temperatures around $10^4$ K and below, metals at low ionization stages emit the observed ion lines.

entries.title: Super-Eddington Neutron Star Accretion Columns: Comparing GRRMHD Simulations with Spectral Models
entries.abstract: The geometry and structure of neutron star accretion columns affect the X-ray emission in super-Eddington accreting systems. We perform four axisymmetric general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of super-Eddington accretion onto magnetized neutron stars with the maximum surface magnetic fields ranging from $3\times10^{10}$ to $1\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{G}$. We measure the column width and estimate the characteristic radiation shock heights from the flow velocity and velocity gradient. Across the four models, the angular width decreases from approximately $0.14$ to $0.07\,\mathrm{rad}$, while the estimated shock height increases from $1.95$ to $3.89\,\mathrm{km}$. We then compare our solutions to the best-fit values derived from spectral modeling of super-Eddington Be/X-ray binary outbursts. We calculate area-equivalent column radii that vary between 5.2 and 3.2 km, three of which fall within the upper part of the range inferred from spectral results using the \texttt{bwcycl} model.

entries.title: On the potential of widening the band of X-ray polarimetry
entries.abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has made X-ray polarimetry a routine astrophysical diagnostic, but its sensitivity is confined to the 2-8 keV band, where the photoelectric effect in a gas is most efficiently exploited. Several of the questions raised by its results, as well as some classical goals of high-energy astrophysics, require polarimetry below 2~keV, to reach the thermal emission of neutron stars, black-hole discs and blazars, and above 8~keV, where reflection, cyclotron lines and the non-thermal emission of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae and magnetars can be isolated. Following a recent review of the subject, we discuss the scientific case for extending the band over roughly 0.1-80 keV and beyond, and the techniques that can deliver it: Bragg diffraction on graded multilayers, photoelectric gas imagers read out by pixel ASICs with time-of-arrival capability, time projection chambers and focal-plane Compton polarimeters, including their combination in stacked focal planes. We then summarise how these techniques are being implemented, or could be, in REDSoX and GOSoX, eXTP, XPP, WXPT and in EXPO and PHEMTO, proposed to the ESA M8 call, as well as in the wide-field transient polarimeter POLAR-2, and we discuss the trade-offs that will drive the design of a wide-band polarimetry mission.

entries.title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
entries.abstract: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

entries.title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
entries.abstract: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. We derive strong constraints using existing X-ray data from NuSTAR. We show that this resonant conversion can lead to $\mathcal O(10^2)$ enhancement in the photon-axion conversion probability, improving the upper limits on axion's photon coupling over part of the mass range where ordinary conversion is suppressed. We also show that this type of resonance predicts distinctive features in the hard X-ray spectrum, which is moderately favored by the data over the background only model, yet it is currently still consistent with statistical fluctuations.

entries.title: TESS discovers an eclipse of the Be star V1294 Aql (= HD 184279) by its not-so-small, low-mass companion
entries.abstract: In a single sector of observations with the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), an eclipse-like event occurred in the Be star V1294 Aql. The reality of the eclipse is corroborated by $UBV$ photometry from the Hvar observatory. The event occurred at phase 17.97 of the linear ephemeris by Harmanec et al. (2022) for the upper conjunction of this SB1 binary (P$_{\rm orb}$ = 192.9 d). Therefore, we conclude that the Be star was eclipsed by its companion. With this elimination of the uncertainty of the orbital inclination, the mass of the secondary is 0.99 to 1.17 M$_\odot$ for masses of the primary from 14 to 18 M$_{\odot}$. The depth of the eclipse of $\sim$6.0% (0.06 mag) is incompatible with a white-dwarf (WD) nature of the companion. At the implied radius of $\sim$25% of that of the B0.5 primary, the secondary is not a bona-fide sdO/sdB star, either, but it could be still in its contraction phase. The increasing number of such stars may lend support to model calculations according to which the timescale of the contraction can be not thermal but instead is governed by the much slower removal of a residual H-rich envelope. It is also possible the companion is on the pre-main sequence in which case the two stars have not yet interacted. Two new interferometric observations were obtained near orbital quadrature but the secondary star was not detected, nor was it detected in high-resolution high-S/N echelle spectra.

entries.title: Multi-Frequency Inversion of Meridional Flows Using Wave-Simulation-Based Sensitivity Kernels: Kernels, Method and Validation On Synthetic Data
entries.abstract: Measuring the solar meridional circulation is central to understanding how magnetic flux and angular momentum are redistributed within the Sun. While time-distance helioseismology has been a primary tool for probing these internal flows, current methods generally rely on broadband travel-time measurements that compress the frequency dependence of the wavefield into single values for each measurement geometry. This approach overlooks the fact that different temporal frequencies sample the solar interior differently, potentially limiting our ability to resolve complex, depth-dependent flow structures. In this paper, we present a framework for performing meridional circulation inversions using frequency-dependent travel-time shifts and corresponding sensitivity kernels derived directly from global-scale, 3D wave-propagation simulations. We analyze sensitivities for horizontal and radial flows, noting that higher temporal frequencies offer increased spatial resolution while their practical application is balanced by the lower signal--to--noise ratio of travel-time measurements at frequencies above the 3 mHz peak of solar oscillations. Using an iterative regularized least-squares solver, we demonstrate that our method successfully recovers many aspects of complex circulation models while remaining robust against the stochastic noise of realistic simulations. We consider the impact of different regularization operators on the inversions, and enforcing constraints like mass conservation to improve inversion results.

entries.title: A Study of Three Intrinsically Luminous Long Period Interacting Eclipsing Binaries in the Galaxy and the Small Magellanic Cloud
entries.abstract: The properties of the eclipsing binaries SMC004701.39-732645.8, SMC005609.41-722809.2 and PW Pup are examined using archival photometric and spectroscopic observations. These systems have orbital periods of hundreds of days, and contain highly evolved components with temperature differences of at least 1000 - 2000K. The SMC systems are among the brightest eclipsing binaries in that galaxy at visible wavelengths, and show excess thermal emission that appears to be typical for luminous K and M giants in that galaxy. A preliminary mass function for SMC004701 suggests a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.8 +/- 0.8 Msolar, whereas the PW Pup mass function indicates a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.2 +/- 0.3 Msolar. Light curve elements are examined for a range of mass ratios using observations at visible and mid-infrared (MIR) wavelengths. The results suggest that SMC004701 may prove to be a double line spectroscopic binary at visible wavelengths. However, with the possible exception of emission from a circumstellar disk, infrared observations will likely be required to detect light from the secondary in the other two systems. All three systems have likely experienced mass transfer, and had components with initial masses that correspond to B spectral types on the main sequence. The light associated with the secondary likely originates from a shell or disk that obscures a hotter central star.

entries.title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
entries.abstract: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to the container. We conclude by discussing the relevance to pulsar glitches.

entries.title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
entries.abstract: We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations. The dataset comprises 5013 individual images, corresponding to 1733 multiply-imaged systems, of which 912 have spectroscopic redshift measurements and 227 are newly identified. Using this new wealth of observations, we construct parametric lens models with our $\mathtt{AstroLensPy}$ software, reproducing the observed image positions with an average image-plane precision $Δ_{\rm RMS}$ of $0.54''$. With a total imaging area of $576$ arcmin$^2$, VENUS offers the largest homogeneous set of cluster strong-lensing models to date. The clusters yield a combined area of $191$ arcmin$^{2}$ magnified by $|μ|\geq3$ for a source $z_s=10$, for example, establishing the VENUS fields as a premier survey for high-redshift studies. Among our sample, the clusters MACS J0717.5+3745, RXC J0600.1-2007 and PLCK G287.0+32.9 display the largest Einstein radii ($\geq 60''$) and magnified areas ($\mathcal{A}_{z_s=10}^{|μ|\geq3} \geq 9$ arcmin$^2$) for a source $z_s=10$, and therefore constitute the most potent gravitational telescopes known to date. Finally, leveraging the statistical power of the sample, we derive scaling relations between various lensing observables (Einstein radius, magnified area, projected mass) and the SZ/X-ray-inferred cluster mass, $M_{500,c}$.
